@about: Solid FEM add-on for PartCraft (0.9 SU.908c). English only. Keys w.* are the warning list (codes of lib/fem/solid-study.js).
name: Solid FEM
panel.honest: A linear static or modal study of this part with the CadCraft finite element library (quadratic tetrahedra). Small displacements, isotropic linear-elastic material; no contact, no yielding. An analysis aid for an engineer, not a design approval.
mat.label: Material
mesh.info: {n} quadratic tetrahedra, {nodes} nodes, {dofs} unknowns, size {h} mm
kind.label: Study
plot.none: There is nothing to plot yet: solve first.
plot.too_big: The plot would need {n} triangles; the limit is 60000. Use a coarser mesh.
plot.shown: Plot placed on the model ({n} colour bands, deformation x{scale}). Blue is the lowest value, red the highest.
plot.stale: The settings changed after this plot was placed; it shows the earlier result. Solve again and place a new plot.
msg.pick: Click faces of the part in the 3D view to add them to {id}, click again to take one off. Press Done picking when finished.
msg.no_faces: This part has no named faces to pick (use the mesh kernel or the exact kernel).
msg.max_faces: At most 64 faces on one item.
msg.no_part: There is no solid part to mesh. Build the part first.
msg.too_fine: An element size that small would make about {n} elements; the limit in the page is {max}. Use a larger size, or run a big model on a workstation.
msg.mesh_big: The mesh has {n} elements; the limit in the page is {max}. Use a larger element size.
msg.done: Solved: largest displacement {d} mm, largest von Mises {s} MPa.
msg.stale: The part changed. Mesh and solve again.
undo.show: Solid FEM: plot on the model
note.liability: Not a code check; your engineer reviews the results.
note.limits: Linear elastic, small displacements, isotropic material. Stress at supports, at load points and at sharp corners depends on the mesh. The numbers are this library's, not those of any other program.
w.too_many: {n} elements is more than the page solves ({max}). Use a larger element size, or run a big model on a workstation.
w.bad_elements: {n} elements have zero or negative volume. Mesh again with a different element size.
w.support_no_faces: Support {id} has no faces on the mesh. Pick its faces again.
w.no_support: Nothing holds the part. Add fixed faces.
w.under_held: The part is not held: {n} of its six rigid-body motions are still free. Add fixed faces so it cannot move or turn.
w.load_no_faces: Load {id} has no faces on the mesh. Pick its faces again.
w.faces_gone: {id}: some of its faces are no longer in the part and were left out.
w.no_load: There is no load: the result is zero.
w.gravity_no_density: Gravity needs a density; this material has none, so gravity adds no load.
w.modal_not_converged: The frequency search did not fully converge; treat the higher modes with care.
w.not_converged: The solver did not converge (residual {res}). The results are not reliable.
w.unbalanced: The support reactions do not balance the loads (relative difference {rel}). Do not rely on the results.
w.coarse: Only {n} elements: a coarse mesh. Refine it (a smaller element size) and compare before relying on the stress.
w.large_disp: The largest displacement is {pct}% of the part's size. This study assumes small displacements; the result is not reliable.
w.over_yield: The largest stress ({vm} MPa) is above the yield stress ({y} MPa). A linear study cannot follow the material past yield; the stress shown is not real.
w.stress_spread: The unsmoothed stress at element nodes ({raw} MPa) is well above the nodal mean ({avg} MPa): the peak is sharp or the mesh is coarse there. Refine and compare.
w.singular: Stress at supports, at load points and at sharp corners grows as the mesh is refined; read it with care.
